Term1: Cmv retinitis and acute retinal necrosis (Navigation)
Text:
# CMV RETINITIS AND ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS

Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.
For sight threatening lesions (lesions within 1500 microns of the fovea) intravitreal infections of ganciclovir or foscarnet are recommended in addition to systemic treatment. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

## Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat retinitis for 14 to 21 days. Patients may be converted to oral therapy after initial intravenous therapy and after clinical improvement of severe disease. Treat acute retinal necrosis with IV therapy for at least 7 days and until disease stabilizes then oral therapy for a minimum of 6 weeks. Maintenance therapy after completion of treatment is indicated when CD4 count <100.
Discontinue maintenance therapy when CD4 count is >100 for 6 months.

Therapy:
## Treatment acute retinal necrosis or severe disease

Intravitreal antiviral in addition to systemic antiviral may provide added therapeutic efficacy.

## Inpatient

Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O]
< OR >
Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O]
Optional add-on therapy for acute retinal necrosis
Ganciclovir 4mg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$$$) [R,O]
< OR >
Foscarnet 2.4mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$$$) [R,O]

## For cases not responsive to Intravenous therapy with foscarnet and ganciclovir used alone

Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O] <AND> foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O]
In cases not responsive to first-line therapy, second-line therapies may be effective. Their use is highly specialized and must be done by someone experienced with HIV/AIDS medicine.

## Treatment of mild to moderate retinitis or after clinical improvement of severe retinitis/acute retinal necrosis

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h($$$) [R,O]

## Maintenance therapy

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q24h ($$$) [R,O]
